name: STM32F722VET6
title: STM32F722xx/STM32F723xx Arm Cortex-M7 microcontrollers with FPU, 216 MHz, up to 512 Kbytes Flash, 256+16+4 Kbytes RAM, USB OTG HS/FS
summary: A Cortex-M7 microcontroller family with FPU, L1 caches and tightly coupled memories, running at up to 216 MHz from a 1.7 V to 3.6 V supply. It has 256 or 512 Kbytes of Flash, 256 Kbytes of system SRAM (64 Kbytes of it DTCM), 16 Kbytes of ITCM and 4 Kbytes of battery-backed SRAM, an external memory controller and Quad-SPI, three 12-bit ADCs, two DACs, up to 18 timers and up to 21 communication interfaces including USB OTG full-speed and high-speed. The STM32F722VET6 is the 512-Kbyte STM32F722 in LQFP100 with 82 I/Os and a ULPI for an external high-speed USB PHY.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M7 with FPU, up to 216 MHz (200 MHz at up to +105 °C)
256 Kbytes system (176 + 16 + 64 DTCM) + 16 Kbytes ITCM + 4 Kbytes backup
OTG FS with PHY; OTG HS with ULPI (STM32F722xx)

pins.name: VBAT
pins.function: Backup supply, 1.65 V to 3.6 V: feeds the RTC, the 32 kHz oscillator, the backup registers and the backup SRAM when VDD is absent. Tie to VDD when the internal reset is off (PDR_ON low).

pins.name: PC13
pins.function: FT I/O. Alternate functions: EVENTOUT. Additional functions: RTC_TAMP1/RTC_TS/RTC_OUT, WKUP4. Fed through the backup power switch, which sinks only 3 mA: as an output it runs at 2 MHz or less into 30 pF or less and is never used as a current source (no LED drive). Takes its main function when the backup domain is first powered; from then on its function follows the RTC registers, which a main reset does not clear.

tables.title: Features and peripheral counts
notes: (1) On LQFP100 the FMC has Bank1 only, which serves one multiplexed NOR/PSRAM memory on chip select NE1.
(2) TIM12 is absent on STM32F723xx packages other than the 176-pin ones, leaving 9 general-purpose timers.
(3) SPI1, SPI2 and SPI3 each work either as SPI or as I2S audio, one at a time.
(4) USB OTG HS uses the ULPI on STM32F722xx and the integrated HS PHY on STM32F723xx.
(5) SDMMC2 has its own supply rail for clock, command and data 0 to 4 from the 144-pin package up.
(6) STM32F723Vx has no SDMMC2.
(7) 216 MHz is the maximum for the –40 °C to +85 °C ambient range; for –40 °C to +105 °C it is 200 MHz.
(8) The 1.7 V minimum of VDD/VDDA needs the internal reset off.
(9) STM32F722xx only.
(10) STM32F723xx only.
Each package line comes with 256 Kbytes or 512 Kbytes of Flash.

circuits.title: STM32F722xx power supply scheme
circuits.description: VBAT takes a 1.65 V to 3.6 V backup source that keeps the backup domain alive through the internal power switch. The VDD pins share twelve 100 nF capacitors and one 4.7 µF, the 4.7 µF on one VDD pin. VCAP_1 and VCAP_2 each carry 2.2 µF for the internal regulator (100 nF each with the regulator bypassed). VDDA, at the VDD potential, takes 100 nF plus 1 µF to VSSA, and VREF+ takes 100 nF plus 1 µF; VREF+ may be tied to VDDA. VSSA is at the VSS potential.

parts.note: twelve, one at each VDD pin
ceramic, at VCAP_1; 100 nF with the regulator off
ceramic, at VCAP_2; 100 nF with the regulator off

notes: On packages that have them, VDDSDMMC (supply of PG[12:9] and PD[7:6]) and VDDUSB (supply of the OTG FS PHY pins) each take 100 nF plus 1 µF.

circuits.title: Typical application with an 8 MHz crystal
circuits.description: An 8 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator across OSC_IN and OSC_OUT, a load capacitor from each side to ground and REXT in series between the crystal and OSC_OUT. The 200 kΩ feedback resistor and the gain stage are inside the part. A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces the crystal and both capacitors.
notes: Crystal and capacitors sit as close to the oscillator pins as they can.

circuits.title: Typical application with a 32.768 kHz crystal
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal or ceramic resonator across OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT, with a load capacitor from each pin to ground. The feedback resistor and the gain stage are inside the part. A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces the crystal and both capacitors.
notes: Crystal and capacitors sit as close to the oscillator pins as they can.

circuits.title: Recommended NRST pin protection
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, placed as close to the chip as possible, guards against stray resets; a push-button to ground is the external reset. The pull-up RPU to VDD is inside the part. The external circuit must be able to bring NRST below VIL(NRST) max.

circuits.title: Typical connection diagram using the ADC
circuits.description: A source VAIN drives an ADC input AINx through its source resistance RAIN; board and pad add a parasitic capacitance to ground. Inside, the pin has protection diodes to VDD and ground (VT about 0.6 V), a leakage of about ±1 µA, and the sample switch RADC into the hold capacitor CADC. RAIN stays within the RAIN max equation.

parts.note: board plus pad, pad about 5 pF

notes: PA0-WKUP (ADC1_IN0, ADC2_IN0, ADC3_IN0) stands for any ADC input.

circuits.title: Power supply and reference decoupling (VREF+ not connected to VDDA)

operation.text: Cortex-M7 core with single-precision FPU, ART Accelerator, 8 Kbytes each of instruction and data L1 cache, MPU and DSP instructions, at up to 216 MHz (462 DMIPS, 2.14 DMIPS/MHz in Dhrystone 2.1). Up to 512 Kbytes of Flash with read and write protection and PCROP, 528 bytes of OTP, 256 Kbytes of system SRAM (64 Kbytes of it data TCM), 16 Kbytes of instruction TCM and 4 Kbytes of backup SRAM kept in the lowest-power modes. FMC for SRAM, PSRAM, SDRAM/LPSDR SDRAM, NOR and NAND with a data bus up to 32 bits; dual-mode Quad-SPI. Application supply and I/Os 1.7 V to 3.6 V, with POR, PDR, PVD and BOR, a dedicated USB supply, a 4 MHz to 26 MHz crystal oscillator, a 16 MHz factory-trimmed RC (1 %), a 32 kHz RTC oscillator with calibration and a 32 kHz internal RC with calibration. Sleep, Stop and Standby modes; VBAT for the RTC, 32 × 32-bit backup registers and the backup SRAM.

Three 12-bit ADCs at 2.4 MSPS with up to 24 channels, 7.2 MSPS when the three interleave; two 12-bit DACs. Up to 18 timers: up to thirteen 16-bit (one a low-power timer that runs in Stop mode) and two 32-bit, each with up to 4 input-capture/output-compare/PWM channels or a pulse counter and quadrature encoder input, 15 of them clocked at up to 216 MHz, plus two watchdogs and SysTick. A 16-stream general-purpose DMA with FIFOs and burst support. SWD and JTAG debug with the Cortex-M7 Trace Macrocell. Up to 140 I/Os with interrupt capability, as many as 136 of them fast (to 108 MHz) and up to 138 5 V tolerant I/Os. Up to 21 communication interfaces: up to 3 I2C (SMBus/PMBus), up to 4 USARTs and 4 UARTs (27 Mbit/s, ISO7816, LIN, IrDA, modem control), up to 5 SPIs (up to 54 Mbit/s), 3 of them with multiplexed simplex I2S clocked from an audio PLL or an external clock, 2 SAIs, 1 CAN 2.0B active and 2 SDMMCs. USB 2.0 full-speed device/host/OTG with on-chip PHY, and a high-speed USB 2.0 OTG controller (also full speed; device, host or OTG) with its own DMA, on-chip full-speed PHY and, by part number, an on-chip high-speed PHY or a ULPI. True random number generator, CRC unit, RTC with subsecond accuracy and hardware calendar, 96-bit unique ID.
LQFP64 (10 × 10 mm), LQFP100 (14 × 14 mm), LQFP144 (20 × 20 mm), LQFP176 (24 × 24 mm), UFBGA144 (7 × 7 mm), UFBGA176 (10 × 10 mm) and WLCSP100 (0.4 mm pitch).

STM32F722xx and STM32F723xx share a Cortex-M7 core at up to 216 MHz with SFPU, DSP instructions and MPU, up to 512 Kbytes of Flash, 256 Kbytes of SRAM including 64 Kbytes of DTCM, 16 Kbytes of ITCM and 4 Kbytes of backup SRAM, joined through a multi-layer AXI interconnect, a 32-bit multi-AHB matrix, two AHB and two APB buses. Every device carries a low-power RTC, two DACs and three 12-bit ADCs, thirteen 16-bit general-purpose timers including two motor-control PWM timers, two 32-bit general-purpose timers and an RNG, plus up to three I2Cs, five SPIs (three with half-duplex I2S on an audio PLL or external clock), four USARTs and four UARTs, USB OTG FS, USB OTG HS (ULPI on STM32F722xx, integrated HS PHY on STM32F723xx), one CAN, two SAIs, two SDMMCs, the FMC and Quad-SPI. They run from –40 °C to +105 °C on 1.7 V to 3.6 V; VDD reaches down to 1.7 V with an external supply supervisor. Separate supply pins for USB (OTG_FS and OTG_HS) and for SDMMC2 (clock, command, 4-bit data) exist on every package except LQFP100 and LQFP64. Seven packages from 64 to 176 pins; the peripheral set depends on the device.

STM32F722xx is pin-to-pin compatible with STM32F7x5xx, STM32F7x6xx and STM32F7x7xx, and with STM32F4xxxx. On LQFP100, pins 19 to 49 differ from STM32F405/407/415/417/427/429/437/439: the VDD on pin 19 is gone, so VSSA through VCAP1 each sit one pin lower (VSSA on 19, VREF+ on 20, VDDA on 21, PA0-WKUP on 22, VSS on 26, VDD on 27, PA4 on 28, VCAP1 on 48) and pin 49 is VSS. On LQFP64, PC5 is gone: PB0, PB1, PB2, PB10 and PB11 sit on pins 25 to 29, VCAP_1 on pin 30 and VSS on 31, so pins 25 to 31 differ from STM32F405/415 and STM32F4x1; pin 47 is VSS where STM32F405/415 has VCAP_2. The single VCAP_1 capacitor is 4.7 µF with ESR from 0.1 Ω to 0.2 Ω (on STM32F4x1, 4.7 µF with ESR of 1 Ω or less). The STM32F722xx LQFP144, UFBGA176 and LQFP176 are fully pin-to-pin compatible with STM32F4xx.

operation.topic: STM32F723xx against STM32F722xx, LQFP144 and LQFP176
operation.text: STM32F723xx drops PG6 and PG7. On LQFP144 the STM32F723xx has OTG_HS_REXT on pin 75 and VDD12OTGHS on pin 76, PB14 and PB15 move to 77 and 78, and PD8 to PG5 shift by two up to pin 92; pins 75 to 92 are not compatible. On LQFP176 the same change puts OTG_HS_REXT on 94 and VDD12OTGHS on 95, with pins 94 to 111 not compatible.

Six-stage dual-issue pipeline with dynamic branch prediction, Harvard caches (8 Kbytes instruction, 8 Kbytes data), a 64-bit AXI4 master, a 64-bit ITCM interface, two 32-bit DTCM interfaces and a low-latency AHB-Lite peripheral port (AHBP). It carries DSP instructions and a single-precision FPU, and is binary compatible with Cortex-M4.

The MPU guards memory from accesses by the wrong task: up to 8 protected regions, each split into up to 8 subregions, sized from 32 bytes to the full 4 Gbytes. An RTOS usually manages it and can change regions per task; an access to a forbidden region is caught. It can be bypassed when not needed.

Up to 512 Kbytes for program and data. Option bytes set the protections: readout protection RDP at level 0 (none), level 1 (no read, erase or program of Flash or backup SRAM while debug is connected or when booting from RAM or the system bootloader) or level 2 (debug and chip readout disabled); write protection WRP against erase and program; and PCROP, which makes user sectors 0 to 7 execute-only by blocking D-bus reads.
Computes a CRC with a configurable generator polynomial and size, for example to check Flash integrity against a link-time signature under EN/IEC 60335-1.

System SRAM of 256 Kbytes: SRAM1 176 Kbytes and SRAM2 16 Kbytes on the AHB bus matrix, and 64 Kbytes of DTCM-RAM on the TCM interface. ITCM-RAM of 16 Kbytes on the TCM interface serves only CPU instruction execution at CPU clock with zero wait states. The DTCM is reachable by the general-purpose and peripheral DMAs through a CPU AHB slave. Backup SRAM of 4 Kbytes is CPU-only, guarded against unwanted writes, and kept in Standby and VBAT modes.

The system has an AXI-to-multi-AHB bridge (three AXI to 32-bit AHB bridges into the bus matrix and one AXI to 64-bit AHB bridge to the Flash) and a 32-bit multi-AHB bus matrix joining the masters (CPU, DMAs, USB HS) to the slaves (Flash, RAM, FMC, Quad-SPI and the AHB/APB peripherals) so that several fast peripherals can work at once.

DMA1 and DMA2 are dual-port general-purpose controllers with 8 streams each, moving data between memories, and between peripherals and memory either way, with FIFOs, burst transfers, circular buffers and double buffering. Each stream has hardware requests and a software trigger; source and destination sizes are independent. Peripherals served: SPI and I2S, I2C, USART, timers, DAC, SDMMC, ADC, SAI and Quad-SPI.

Three controllers: NOR/PSRAM, NAND, and synchronous DRAM (SDRAM/Mobile LPSDR SDRAM). It drives SRAM, NOR/OneNAND Flash, PSRAM (4 banks), NAND Flash with hardware ECC over up to 8 Kbytes, and SDRAM, on an 8-, 16- or 32-bit data bus, with a chip select and configuration per bank, a write FIFO and an SDRAM read FIFO. FMC_CLK/FMC_SDCLK for synchronous accesses runs at HCLK/2 at most. It also drives parallel LCD controllers in Intel 8080 and Motorola 6800 modes. On LQFP100 only Bank1 is present, for one multiplexed NOR/PSRAM on NE1.

Interface to single, dual or quad SPI Flash in direct (register) mode, status-polling mode or memory-mapped mode, where up to 256 Mbytes of external Flash appear in the memory map for 8-, 16- and 32-bit reads and code execution. Opcode and frame format are programmable, in single or double data rate.
16 priority levels and up to 110 maskable interrupt channels in addition to the 16 Cortex-M7 interrupt lines, with low-latency entry, late-arrival handling, tail chaining and automatic state saving.

24 edge-detector lines, each with its own rising, falling or both-edge trigger and mask, and a pending register. A pulse shorter than one APB2 clock period is caught. Up to 140 GPIOs (STM32F722xx) or 138 (STM32F723xx) map onto the 16 external interrupt lines.

Out of reset the CPU runs from the 16 MHz HSI RC, factory-trimmed to 1 %. The system clock can then be the HSI or an external 4 MHz to 26 MHz source, which is monitored: on failure the clock falls back to the HSI and an interrupt can fire. The main PLL takes either source up to 216 MHz, with its own interrupt handling. The two AHB buses run at up to 216 MHz, the APB2 (high-speed) domain at up to 108 MHz and the APB1 (low-speed) domain at up to 54 MHz. PLLI2S and PLLSAI give I2S and SAI master clocks for every standard rate from 8 kHz to 192 kHz. STM32F723xx adds PLL1 and PLL2 inside the USB HS PHY controller: PLL1, fed by the HSE, makes 60 MHz for PLL2, which makes the 480 Mbit/s high-speed clock.

At start-up the BOOT pin and the BOOT_ADDx option bytes pick the boot address anywhere from 0x0000 0000 to 0x3FFF FFFF: Flash on ITCM or AXIM, the ITCM, DTCM and AXIM SRAMs, or the system-memory bootloader, which reprograms the Flash over a serial interface.

VDD 1.7 V to 3.6 V feeds the I/Os and the internal regulator. VDDA and VSSA, 1.7 V to 3.6 V, feed the ADC, DAC, reset blocks, RCs and PLL and go to VDD and VSS. VBAT, 1.65 V to 3.6 V, feeds the RTC, the 32 kHz oscillator and the backup registers through a power switch when VDD is absent. The 1.7 V minimum on VDD/VDDA needs the internal reset off.

VDDSDMMC feeds the SDMMC2 clock, command and 4-bit data pins from VDD or a separate 1.8 V to 3.6 V supply (for example 2.7 V while the device runs at 1.8 V). A separate supply must come up last and go first, stay below VDD while VDD is under its minimum at power-on and power-down, and respect its rise and fall rates; in operation it may sit above or below VDD, and its I/Os then work between VDDSDMMC minimum and maximum.

VDDUSB feeds the USB transceivers from VDD or a separate 3.0 V to 3.6 V supply (for example 3.3 V while the device runs at 1.8 V). A separate supply must come up last and go first, stay below VDD while VDD is under its minimum at power-on and power-down, and respect its rise and fall rates; in operation it may sit above or below VDD. With USB in use its I/Os work between VDDUSB minimum and maximum; one VDDUSB feeds both the OTG_HS and OTG_FS transceivers, so the I/Os of an unused one stay on VDDUSB; with USB unused they work between VDD minimum and maximum.
On STM32F7x3xx the USB OTG HS PHY regulator puts out 1.2 V on VDD12OTGHS, which needs an external 2.2 µF capacitor.

With PDR_ON high (or on packages without PDR_ON) the supervisor is always on. POR/PDR is active from power-on and works from 1.8 V; above that threshold the option bytes load and confirm, change or permanently disable the BOR thresholds (three are available). The device stays in reset while VDD is below VPOR/PDR or VBOR with no external reset circuit. The software-enabled PVD compares VDD/VDDA with VPVD and can interrupt when the supply falls below or rises above it.

On packages with PDR_ON, tying PDR_ON to VSS turns off the internal POR/PDR. An external supervisor then watches VDD and holds NRST low while VDD is below 1.7 V. In this mode POR/PDR and PVD are off, BOR must be disabled, and VBAT is unusable, so VBAT goes to VDD. Packages with a PDR_ON pin offer it; LQFP64 and LQFP100 do not.

Regulator ON has three software-set modes. Main regulator (MR) serves Run and Sleep, in normal mode or in over-drive, which allows a higher frequency at a given voltage scaling; in Stop it runs normal or under-drive (lower leakage). The low-power regulator (LPR) serves Stop, likewise normal or under-drive. Power-down serves Standby: the regulator output goes high-impedance, the core domain is unpowered and registers and SRAM are lost. VCAP_1 and VCAP_2 need 2 × 2.2 µF with ESR below 2 Ω, or 1 × 4.7 µF with ESR from 0.1 Ω to 0.2 Ω where only VCAP_1 exists (LQFP64). On packages with BYPASS_REG the regulator is on while BYPASS_REG is low; every package has regulator ON.

Only on packages with BYPASS_REG, held high. An external V12 supply then feeds VCAP_1 and VCAP_2, set to suit the target frequency because voltage scaling is no longer internal, and the two 2.2 µF capacitors become two 100 nF decoupling capacitors. V12 is no longer monitored internally: an external supervisor watches it and drives PA0 as the V12-domain power-on reset, so PA0 is not a GPIO; while PA0 is low, debug under power-on reset is impossible, so PA0 and NRST are handled separately when debug under reset is needed. Over-drive, under-drive and Standby are unavailable. VDD must always exceed VCAP_1 and VCAP_2. If VCAP reaches its V12 minimum before VDD reaches 1.7 V, PA0 is held low until both have; if VCAP is slower, PA0 may be asserted low externally; if VCAP falls below its minimum while VDD is above 1.7 V, PA0 must be asserted. The V12 minimum depends on the target frequency. LQFP64 has no VCAP_2.

operation.topic: RTC, backup SRAM and backup registers
operation.text: The RTC counts in BCD on its own: calendar with subseconds, seconds, minutes, hours (12 or 24 h), weekday, date, month and year with automatic month-length and leap-year correction; two programmable alarms; on-the-fly correction of 1 to 32767 RTC clock pulses; reference-clock detection from a 50 Hz or 60 Hz source; digital calibration with 0.95 ppm resolution; three tamper pins with programmable filter; timestamp on the timestamp pin, a tamper event or a switch to VBAT; and a 17-bit auto-reload wake-up timer. The RTC and the 32 backup registers (128 bytes, not cleared by system or power reset or by wake-up from Standby) run from VDD when present, otherwise from VBAT through a switch. RTC clock: a 32.768 kHz crystal or an external resonator or oscillator (LSE), the 32 kHz LSI RC, or HSE divided by 32. On LSE the RTC works in VBAT mode and every low-power mode; on LSI it works in the low-power modes but not in VBAT mode. Alarm, wake-up timer, timestamp and tamper events can interrupt and wake the device.

Sleep: the CPU stops, peripherals run and an interrupt or event wakes the CPU. Stop: SRAM and registers are kept, all 1.2 V domain clocks stop and the PLL, HSI and HSE are off; the regulator is MR or LPR, each normal or under-drive; any EXTI line wakes it (the 16 external lines, PVD, RTC alarm, wake-up, tamper or timestamp, USB OTG FS/HS wake-up, LPTIM1 asynchronous interrupt). Standby: the regulator and the whole 1.2 V domain are off along with the PLL, HSI and HSE; SRAM and registers are lost except the backup domain and, if selected, the backup SRAM. Standby ends on an NRST reset, an IWDG reset, a wake-up pin edge (6 pins: PA0, PA2, PC1, PC13, PI8, PI11) or an RTC event (alarm, wake-up, tamper, timestamp). Standby is unavailable when the regulator is bypassed and an external supply drives the 1.2 V domain.

VBAT, from a battery, a supercapacitor or VDD, takes over the RTC, backup registers and backup SRAM when VDD is absent. External interrupts and RTC alarms or events do not end VBAT operation. With PDR_ON at VSS (internal reset off) VBAT is unusable and goes to VDD.
Timer set: TIM1 and TIM8 (advanced-control), ten general-purpose timers, TIM6 and TIM7 (basic), plus the independent and window watchdogs; every counter can freeze in debug mode.

Three-phase PWM generators on 6 channels with complementary outputs and programmable dead time, or full general-purpose timers. Their 4 channels do input capture, output compare, edge- or centre-aligned PWM and one-pulse output; as 16-bit PWM generators they modulate 0 % to 100 %. They link to the other timers for synchronisation or event chaining and have their own DMA requests.

TIM2 and TIM5 have a 32-bit, and TIM3 and TIM4 a 16-bit, auto-reload up/down counter with a 16-bit prescaler and 4 channels, each doing capture, compare, PWM or one-pulse, giving up to 16 such channels on the largest packages. They link to each other and to TIM1/TIM8, have their own DMA requests, and read quadrature encoders and 1 to 4 Hall sensors. TIM9 to TIM14 have a 16-bit auto-reload up counter and 16-bit prescaler; TIM10, TIM11, TIM13 and TIM14 have one channel and TIM9 and TIM12 two, for capture, compare, PWM or one-pulse output; they synchronise with TIM2 to TIM5 or serve as time bases.
Mainly the DAC trigger and waveform generator, or a 16-bit time base, each with its own DMA request.

Has its own clock and keeps counting in Stop mode on LSE, LSI or an external clock, from which it can wake the device. 16-bit up counter with 16-bit auto-reload and compare registers, pulse or PWM output, continuous or one-shot, software or hardware trigger, clock from LSE, LSI, HSI, APB or an external input (counting even with no internal clock running), a programmable glitch filter and encoder mode.
12-bit down counter with 8-bit prescaler on its own 32 kHz RC, so it runs in Stop and Standby; resets the device or serves as a free-running timeout timer; hardware or software start by option byte.
7-bit down counter on the main clock, free-running if wanted, with an early-warning interrupt and freeze in debug mode.
24-bit down counter with auto-reload, a maskable interrupt at zero and a programmable clock source, meant for an RTOS.

Three I2C interfaces, I2C-bus rev. 5 compatible: master and slave, multimaster, Standard-mode to 100 kbit/s, Fast-mode to 400 kbit/s, Fast-mode Plus to 1 Mbit/s with 20 mA I/O drive, addressing in 7 or 10 bits with multiple 7-bit own addresses, setup and hold times set by software, and clock stretching that can be turned off. SMBus 2.0 (hardware PEC with ACK control, ARP, SMBus alert) and PMBus 1.1. An independent clock keeps the bus speed fixed when PCLK changes; noise filtering both analog and digital; a one-byte buffer served by DMA.

USART1/2/3/6 and UART4/5/7/8: full-duplex asynchronous with oversampling by 16 or 8, a dual clock domain, baud rates up to 27 Mbit/s from a 216 MHz system clock with oversampling by 8, auto baud detection, 7-, 8- or 9-bit words, MSB or LSB first, odd, even or no parity, 1, 1.5 or 2 stop bits, single-wire half duplex, separate TX and RX polarity, swappable TX/RX, modem and RS-485 flow control, multiprocessor mode, LIN break, IrDA SIR (3/16 bit), Modbus. USART1/2/3/6 add synchronous mode with clock output and smartcard mode (ISO/IEC 7816-3 T=0 and T=1).

Up to five SPIs, master or slave, full duplex or simplex: SPI1, SPI4 and SPI5 up to 50 Mbit/s, SPI2 and SPI3 up to 25 Mbit/s; a 3-bit prescaler gives 8 master clocks; frames of 4 to 16 bits; NSS pulse mode, TI mode, hardware CRC; all on DMA. Three I2S interfaces share SPI1, SPI2 and SPI3: master or slave, simplex, 16- or 32-bit, input or output, 8 kHz to 192 kHz, with a master clock output of 256 × the sample rate; all on DMA.

Two serial audio interfaces, each with two independent sub-blocks that transmit or receive through their FIFOs: protocols I2S, MSB- or LSB-justified, TDM, PCM/DSP, AC'97 and SPDIF out, at 8 kHz to 192 kHz, master or slave, with a 256 × fs master clock output in master mode. The two sub-blocks can run synchronously for full duplex. Both SAIs are on DMA.

PLLI2S gives the I2S and SAI an accurate sample clock without disturbing the CPU or USB clocks and can change rate without stopping the main PLL, covering 8 kHz to 192 kHz with very low error; a master clock input pin can also lock I2S/SAI to an external PLL or codec. PLLSAI clocks SAI1 when PLLI2S is busy on the other audio family (49.152 MHz or 11.2896 MHz) and both rates are needed at once.

SDMMC hosts follow MultiMediaCard System Specification 4.2 with 1-, 4- and 8-bit buses, transfer at up to 50 MHz, and comply with SD Memory Card Specification 2.0 (1- and 4-bit). One SD/SDMMC/MMC4.2 card at a time, or a stack of MMC4.1 or earlier. DMA capable.

bxCAN, 2.0A and 2.0B active, up to 1 Mbit/s, standard 11-bit and extended 29-bit identifiers, three transmit mailboxes, two 3-stage receive FIFOs and 28 shared scalable filter banks; 256 bytes of SRAM belong to the CAN.

USB 2.0 and OTG 2.0 device/host/OTG with integrated transceivers and PHY: 1.28 Kbytes of shared, dynamically sized Rx/Tx FIFO, SRP and HNP, 1 bidirectional control endpoint plus 5 IN and 5 OUT endpoints, 12 host channels that support periodic OUT, OTG1.3 or OTG2.0 by software, LPM, BCD, no external resistors needed. Needs a 48 MHz clock from a PLL on the HSE. OTG and host modes need a power switch when bus-powered devices are connected.

USB 2.0 and OTG 2.0 device/host/OTG at up to 480 Mbit/s with an integrated full-speed (12 Mbit/s) transceiver. STM32F722xx reaches high speed through an external PHY on its ULPI (12 signals, SDR, clocked from its 60 MHz output); STM32F723xx has an integrated HS PHY. 4 Kbytes of dynamically sized FIFO, 8 bidirectional endpoints, 16 host channels that support periodic OUT, SRP/HNP, OTG1.3/OTG2.0, LPM, its own DMA, no external resistors. Needs a 48 MHz clock from a PLL on the HSE, and a power switch for bus-powered devices in OTG or host mode. On STM32F723xx the USBPHYC sets the PHY PLL1/PLL2 values, the other PHY controls, and controls and monitors the PHY LDO.
Delivers 32-bit random numbers from an integrated analog source.

Each pin is set as input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), as output (push-pull or open-drain, optionally pulled up or down) or as an alternate function; most share digital or analog functions. All are high-current capable with selectable speed. A locking sequence freezes a pin's configuration. Fast I/O toggles at up to 108 MHz.

Three 12-bit ADCs sharing up to 16 external channels, single-shot or scan, with simultaneous and interleaved sample-and-hold, DMA, and an analog watchdog on one, several or all channels that interrupts outside programmed limits. TIM1, TIM2, TIM3, TIM4, TIM5 or TIM8 can trigger conversions.

Gives a voltage linear in temperature over a 1.7 V to 3.6 V conversion range, on ADC1_IN18 shared with VBAT; with both enabled only VBAT converts. Its offset varies between chips, so it suits measuring temperature changes; an external sensor serves absolute readings.

Two buffered 12-bit channels, each its own converter: 8- or 12-bit monotonic output, left or right alignment in 12-bit mode, synchronised update, noise and triangle waves, independent or simultaneous conversion, DMA per channel, external triggers, reference VREF+. Eight trigger inputs; the channels trigger from timer update outputs, which also drive DMA streams.

SWJ-DP combines JTAG and serial-wire debug: SWD uses 2 pins instead of the 5 of JTAG, JTMS/SWDIO and JTCK/SWCLK are shared, and a sequence on TMS switches between JTAG-DP and SW-DP; unused JTAG pins can serve as GPIO. The Embedded Trace Macrocell streams compressed instruction and data trace through a few ETM pins to an external trace port analyser.

The 4-Gbyte space is eight 512-Mbyte blocks: block 0 holds ITCM RAM, system memory, Flash on the ITCM and AXIM interfaces and the option bytes; block 1 the DTCM, SRAM1 and SRAM2; block 2 the APB1, APB2, AHB1 and AHB2 peripherals; blocks 3 to 6 the FMC banks and Quad-SPI on AHB3; block 7 the Cortex-M7 internal peripherals. The same Flash appears at 0x0020 0000 on ITCM and at 0x0800 0000 on AXIM.

Voltages are measured from VSS unless a table says otherwise. Min and max limits hold over the worst case of ambient temperature, supply and frequency; they are tested on every device at TA = 25 °C and at TA = TAmax of the chosen temperature range. Limits marked in a footnote as coming from characterization, design simulation or technology data are mean ± 3σ of a sample. Typical figures are at TA = 25 °C and VDD = 3.3 V (for the 1.7 V to 3.6 V range), are design guidance and are not tested; typical ADC accuracy is the value that 95 % of a characterization batch meets over the full temperature range (mean ± 2σ). Typical curves are design guidance, not tested. Pin figures are measured with 50 pF from the pin to ground; an input voltage is applied to a pin from a source referred to ground.

On the STM32F722xx: VBAT takes a 1.65 V to 3.6 V backup source that feeds the backup domain (32 kHz oscillator, RTC, wakeup logic, backup registers and backup RAM) through the internal power switch. VDDSDMMC (supply of PG[12:9] and PD[7:6]) takes 100 nF plus 1 µF. The VDD pins take twelve 100 nF capacitors plus one 4.7 µF, the 4.7 µF on one VDD pin. VCAP_1 and VCAP_2 each take 2.2 µF; with the regulator off (bypassed) these become 100 nF. VDDUSB (supply of the OTG FS PHY pins) takes 100 nF plus 1 µF. VDDA takes 100 nF plus 1 µF and VREF+ 100 nF plus 1 µF; VDDA is at the VDD potential and VSSA at VSS. On the STM32F723xx, VDDUSB supplies both the FS PHY pins (PA11/PA12) and the HS PHY pins (PB14/PB15), VDD12OTGHS takes 2.2 µF and OTG_HS_REXT takes a 3 kΩ ±1 % resistor to ground. Each supply pair (VDD/VSS, VDDA/VSSA and so on) has its ceramic capacitors as close to its pins as possible, or under them on the far side of the board; leaving them out to save space or cost can make the part misbehave.
Supply current is measured as IDD into the VDD and VDDA pins together and as IDD_VBAT into the VBAT pin.

Stress beyond the figures in the voltage, current and thermal rating tables can damage the part for good; they are stress limits, not operating conditions, and long exposure to them can shorten its life. The mission profile follows JEDEC JESD47; longer profiles are offered on request.

The main regulator is stabilised by an external capacitor CEXT on the VCAP pins, modelled as a capacitance with an equivalent series resistance (ESR) and a leakage resistance. LQFP64 has no VCAP2 pin and uses one 4.7 µF capacitor on VCAP1 instead of the two 2.2 µF parts. With the regulator bypassed, the VCAP capacitors are replaced by two 100 nF decoupling capacitors.
Turning over-drive on or off stalls the system clock while the internal voltage settles; the switch times are in the over-drive switching table.

Supply current depends on supply voltage, ambient temperature, pin loading, software configuration, clock frequencies, pin toggle rates, where the program sits in memory and the code itself. Run-mode figures use a reduced code whose current matches CoreMark. For the typical and maximum tables: every I/O is an input held at VDD or VSS with no load; peripherals are off unless a row says otherwise; Flash wait states suit fHCLK and the VDD range; with the regulator on, Scale 3 is used up to 144 MHz, Scale 2 above 144 MHz up to 168 MHz and Scale 1 above 168 MHz up to 216 MHz, with over-drive on only at 216 MHz; with the regulator off V12 comes from outside per the general operating conditions; fPCLK1 = fHCLK/4 and fPCLK2 = fHCLK/2; the external clock is 25 MHz with the PLL on above 25 MHz. Typical values hold for 1.7 V ≤ VDD ≤ 3.6 V at TA = 25 °C, maximum values for the same range at the maximum TA, unless a table says otherwise. Over 1.7 V ≤ VDD ≤ 3.6 V the frequency limit is 180 MHz.

I/O current has a static and a dynamic part. Static: an input with its pull-up draws current when held low outside, set by the pull resistor values in the I/O static characteristics; an output also feeds any external pull-down or load. An input held at a voltage between the logic levels draws current through its Schmitt trigger; setting such a pin, an ADC input for one, to analog mode avoids it. A floating input can drift to a middle level or toggle from noise, so an unused pin is set to analog mode or held at a defined level by a pull resistor or as an output. Dynamic: a switching pin draws supply current for its own circuitry and to charge and discharge its load capacitance, internal and external. The switching figures are for a push-pull output toggled by software at a fixed rate, with the pad and board capacitance CINT + CS taken as 15 pF.

Each peripheral's figure is the rise in supply current when that peripheral alone is clocked, against all peripherals clocked off, with I/Os in analog input state from start-up, the I/O compensation cell on, ART/L1 cache on, Scale 1 with V12 = 1.32 V, fPCLK1 = fHCLK/4 and fPCLK2 = fHCLK/2, at 25 °C and VDD = 3.3 V. fHCLK is 216 MHz in Scale 1 with over-drive, 168 MHz in Scale 2 and 144 MHz in Scale 3.

On the STM32F723xx, the OTG HS controller and its HS PHY together draw the current in the USB HS table: the difference between USB configured with no transfer and USB configured with a transfer running, the part enumerated as a HID device, at 25 °C with VDD = VDDUSB = 3.3 V, and fHCLK of 216 MHz (Scale 1 with over-drive), 168 MHz (Scale 2) or 144 MHz (Scale 3).

Wakeup time runs from the wakeup trigger to the first instruction the CPU executes. Sleep and Stop are exited by a WFE wakeup event; the WKUP pin (PA0) wakes the part from Standby, Stop and Sleep. Figures are at VDD = 3.3 V.

In HSE or LSE bypass mode the oscillator is off and OSC_IN (or OSC32_IN) is an ordinary I/O input that takes a clock from outside; the clock meets the I/O static characteristics. The HSE and LSE external clock tables come from tests with such a source over the ambient and supply ranges of the general operating conditions. The AC timing figures define the clock by its high and low levels VHSEH/VHSEL (VLSEH/VLSEL), the high and low times tw, the rise and fall times tr and tf, and the period T.

The HSE oscillator runs a 4 MHz to 26 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator; its figures come from characterization with the typical external parts in the HSE oscillator table. Crystal and load capacitors sit as close to the oscillator pins as they can, to keep distortion and start-up settling short. CL1 and CL2 are good ceramic parts for high frequencies, typically 5 pF to 25 pF, chosen for the crystal and normally equal; the crystal's rated load capacitance is their series value, with the pin and board capacitance counted in (about 10 pF together as a first estimate). The feedback resistor RF (200 kΩ typ) is inside; REXT in series with OSC_OUT depends on the crystal. ST's application note AN2867 covers crystal selection.

The LSE oscillator runs a 32.768 kHz crystal or ceramic resonator, with a load capacitor from each pin to ground; the feedback resistor is inside. Its figures come from characterization with typical external parts. Crystal and capacitors sit as close to the oscillator pins as they can. The drive level is set by LSEDRV[1:0]: 00 low, 10 medium low, 01 medium high, 11 high.

Spread spectrum clock generation (SSCG) lowers electromagnetic emission and exists on the main PLL only. The modulation is set by a period MODEPER and an increment step INCSTEP. Because both are rounded to whole numbers, the achieved modulation depth is quantized. Worked example: with fPLL_IN = 1 MHz and fMod = 1 kHz, MODEPER = 250; with md = ±2 % (4 % peak to peak) and PLLN = 240, INCSTEP = 126 and the quantized depth is 2.002 % (peak). In center spread the output frequency swings between F0 + md and F0 - md around the nominal fPLL_OUT F0; in down spread it swings between F0 and F0 - 2 × md. One modulation period is tmode.
Flash figures hold for TA = -40 °C to 105 °C unless stated. Parts leave the factory with the Flash erased. VPP is connected only while programming or erasing.

Susceptibility is tested on samples during characterization, with the part running a simple program that toggles two LEDs; the LEDs show a failure, and a reset brings normal operation back. ESD (both polarities) goes to every pin until the function is disturbed, per IEC 61000-4-2; fast transient bursts (both polarities) go to VDD and VSS through 100 pF, per IEC 61000-4-4. Levels and classes follow ST application note AN1709. A series resistor of 1 kΩ as close to the MCU as possible is advised on pins exposed to noise, those on traces longer than 50 mm. EMC is characterised at component level with simple software; the result in an application depends strongly on its software, so EMC software measures and pre-qualification tests at the needed level are advised. Software handles runaway conditions: a corrupted program counter, an unexpected reset, corrupted critical data such as control registers. Most common failures (unexpected reset, program counter corruption) can be provoked by holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 s, and ESD can be applied to the part within its ratings; software is then hardened against unrecoverable errors (ST application note AN1015). Emission is measured while the part runs EEMBC code, per IEC 61967-2, which defines the test board and pin loading.

ESD: a positive then a negative pulse 1 s apart go to the pins of each sample for every pin combination; the sample is 3 parts × (n + 1) supply pins, per ANSI/ESDA/JEDEC JS-001-2012 and ANSI/ESD S5.3.1-2009. Static latch-up: six parts take a supply overvoltage on each supply pin and current injected into every I/O pin, per EIA/JESD 78A.

Current forced into I/O pins by voltages below VSS or above VDD (on standard 3 V pins) is to be avoided in normal use. Robustness against accidental injection is tested on samples during characterization: current is injected into one floating-input pin at a time while a simple program runs, and a failure is a parameter out of range (ADC error above 5 LSB TUE, induced leakage on neighbouring pins outside -5 µA/+0 µA) or another functional fault such as a reset or an oscillator frequency shift. Negative injection induces negative leakage, positive injection positive leakage. A Schottky diode from pin to ground is advised on analog pins that may see negative current.

Every I/O is CMOS and TTL compliant with no software setting, and covers more than the bare CMOS or TTL levels. The I/O static figures come from tests over the general operating conditions unless stated.

Between the design-simulation thresholds (VILmax = 0.35VDD - 0.04 and VIHmin = 0.45VDD + 0.3) the input state is not determined. Production tests check the CMOS levels, VILmax = 0.3VDD and VIHmin = 0.7VDD; from VDD = 2.7 V the TTL levels VILmax = 0.8 V and VIHmin = 2 V are met as well.

GPIOs sink or source up to ±8 mA, and up to ±20 mA with relaxed VOL/VOH. PC13, PC14, PC15 and PI8 sink or source up to ±3 mA; as outputs they run at no more than 2 MHz into at most 30 pF. The number of pins driving current is kept within the absolute maximum ratings: the current sourced by all I/Os on VDD plus the MCU's maximum Run current on VDD stays within ΣIVDD, and on the ground side, the I/O sink current plus the maximum Run current stays within ΣIVSS. The output voltage figures hold over the general operating conditions unless stated.

An output's rise time tr(IO)out runs from 10 % to 90 % of its swing and its fall time tf(IO)out from 90 % to 10 %. The maximum frequency is reached when (tr + tf) ≤ 2/3 T, T being the period, with a duty cycle of 45 % to 55 % into the load CL given in the I/O AC table.

The NRST input is a CMOS input with a permanent pull-up RPU to VDD, followed inside by a Schmitt trigger and a filter. A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, as close to the chip as possible, guards against stray resets; an external reset circuit such as a push-button to ground can share the pin. Whatever drives NRST must pull it below VIL(NRST) max, or the reset is not taken.

Timer figures are guaranteed by design; the I/O port characteristics cover the timer pin functions (capture, compare, external clock input, PWM). With the TIMPRE bit in RCC_DCKCFGR set, timers on APB1 or APB2 run at up to 216 MHz: TIMxCLK = HCLK when the APBx prescaler is 1, 2 or 4, and 4 × PCLKx otherwise.

Negative current injected into any analog input badly degrades a conversion running on another analog input; a Schottky diode from pin to ground is advised on analog pins that may see it. Positive injection within the IINJ(PIN) and ΣIINJ(PIN) limits leaves accuracy unchanged. Error terms: ET, the largest gap between the actual and ideal transfer curves; EO, how far the first real code transition sits from the first ideal one; EG, how far the final real transition sits from the final ideal one; ED, the largest gap between an actual step and the ideal step; EL, the largest gap between any actual transition and the line joining the end points. One ideal LSB is VREF+/4096 (or VDDA/4096, depending on the package). The parasitic capacitance at an input (board, solder, and about 5 pF of pad) costs accuracy when large; lowering fADC wins it back.

VDDA and VREF+ are decoupled each by 1 µF in parallel with 10 nF to VSSA/VREF-, or, with VREF+ tied to VDDA, by one 1 µF and 10 nF pair on the joined pin. The 10 nF parts are good ceramic capacitors placed as close to the chip as possible. Every package but LQFP64 has a VREF+ pin; only UFBGA176 and UFBGA144 have VREF-, which elsewhere is tied inside to VSSA.

Each 12-bit DAC output has a buffer that lowers the output impedance so that external loads can be driven with no op amp; setting BOFFx in DAC_CR bypasses it. Loads are specified as RL and CL in parallel from DAC_OUTx to ground.

The I2C interface meets the I2C-bus specification (user manual rev. 03) in Standard-mode (up to 100 kbit/s), Fast-mode (up to 400 kbit/s) and Fast-mode Plus (up to 1 Mbit/s). Its timings hold by design once the peripheral is set up as the RM0385 reference manual describes and I2CCLK is above the minimum in the I2CCLK table. SDA and SCL are not true open-drain: in open-drain mode the PMOS to VDD is switched off but still there. The 20 mA output drive of Fast-mode Plus is not supported, which caps the load Cload in Fm+ through Tr(SDA/SCL) = 0.8473 × Rp × Cload and Rp(min) = (VDD - VOL(max)) / IOL(max), Rp being the bus pull-up. Every SDA and SCL pin has an analog spike filter.

SPI timings hold over the general operating conditions with OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11, a 30 pF load and measurements at 0.5VDD; the I/O port characteristics cover the NSS, SCK, MOSI and MISO pins. SPI1 with SCK on PA5 reaches 40 MHz at most. The slave transmitter's top frequency is set by tv(SO) plus the master's tsu(MI), which together fit in the SCK phase before the sampling edge; the figure assumes a master with tsu(MI) = 0 and a 50 % SCK duty cycle.

I2S timings hold over the general operating conditions with OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 10, a 30 pF load and measurements at 0.5VDD; the I/O port characteristics cover the CK, SD and WS pins. fMCK, fCK and DCK reflect the digital peripheral only and shift slightly with the source clock's precision. DCK depends mostly on the ODD bit: the digital part alone gives a minimum of I2SDIV/(2 × I2SDIV + ODD) and a maximum of (I2SDIV + ODD)/(2 × I2SDIV + ODD). The FS maximum holds in every mode and condition. RM0385's I2S section covers the sampling frequency. In the Philips-protocol timing, the LSB sent or received first is that of the previous byte; none goes out before the first byte.

SAI timings hold over the general operating conditions with OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 10, a 30 pF load and measurements at 0.5VDD; the I/O port characteristics cover the SCK, SD and WS pins. The APB clock is at least twice the SAI clock.

Both the OTG HS and the OTG FS controllers have this full-speed interface. The transceiver works down to VDDUSB = 2.7 V, but its full-speed electrical figures degrade between 2.7 V and 3.0 V. With VBUS sensing on, PA9 and PB13 stay in their default floating-input state rather than an alternate function, and the sensing block draws about 200 µA on them. DP (D+) and DM (D-) need no external series resistors: the driver has its matching impedance built in. Rise and fall times run from 10 % to 90 % of the data signal (USB 2.0 specification, chapter 7); VCRS is the crossover voltage of the differential lines.

On the STM32F722xx, USB high speed runs through an external ULPI PHY. The ULPI timings hold over the general operating conditions with OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11 and a 20 pF load unless a row says otherwise, measured at 0.5VDD; fHCLK is at least 30 MHz. The ULPI clock times control in (ULPI_DIR, ULPI_NXT) and data in by setup tSC/tSD and hold tHC/tHD, and control out (ULPI_STP) and data out by the output delays tDC/tDD.
The STM32F723xx has a high-speed USB PHY on chip; its DC and driver figures follow.
The CANx_TX and CANx_RX pins follow the I/O port characteristics.

FMC timings hold over the general operating conditions with OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11 and measurements at 0.5VDD; the I/O port characteristics cover the pins. THCLK (Thclk) is the HCLK period. Asynchronous timings use AddressSetupTime = 0x1, AddressHoldTime = 0x1, DataSetupTime = 0x1 (0x5 in asynchronous NWAIT mode), BusTurnAroundDuration = 0x0 and CL = 30 pF. In the asynchronous waveforms FMC_NADV is used in modes 2/B, C and D only, not in mode 1.

Synchronous timings use BurstAccessMode enabled, MemoryType CRAM, WriteBurst enabled, CLKDivision = 1, DataLatency = 1 for NOR Flash and 0 for PSRAM, 30 pF on data and address lines and 10 pF on FMC_CLK unless stated. FMC_CLK reaches 108 MHz with 20 pF or 90 MHz with 30 pF on it for 2.7 V ≤ VDD ≤ 3.6 V, and 70 MHz with 10 pF for 1.71 V ≤ VDD < 2.7 V.

NAND timings use COM and ATT SetupTime = 0x01, WaitSetupTime = 0x03, HoldSetupTime = 0x02 and HiZSetupTime = 0x01, bank FMC_Bank_NAND, a 16-bit data width, ECC on with 512-byte pages, TCLRSetupTime = 0 and TARSetupTime = 0.

SDRAM timings use 30 pF on data and address lines and 10 pF on FMC_SDCLK unless stated. FMC_SDCLK reaches 100 MHz with 20 pF on it for 3.0 V ≤ VDD ≤ 3.6 V, 90 MHz with 30 pF for 2.7 V ≤ VDD ≤ 3.6 V, and 70 MHz with 10 pF for 1.71 V ≤ VDD < 1.9 V.

Quad-SPI timings hold over the general operating conditions (ambient temperature, fAHB and VDD) with OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11, a 20 pF load and measurements at 0.5VDD; the I/O port characteristics cover the pins. DDR mode gives separate rising-edge and falling-edge input and output times (tsf, thr/thf, tvr/tvf).

SDMMC timings hold over the general operating conditions (ambient temperature, fPCLK2 and VDD) with OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11, a 30 pF load and measurements at 0.5VDD; the I/O port characteristics cover the pins. In high-speed mode CMD and D inputs are referred to CK by tISU/tIH and outputs by tOV/tOH; in SD default mode by tISUD/tIHD and tOVD/tOHD. The eMMC figures are for VDD = 1.71 V to 1.9 V with a 20 pF load.

The top side carries the product identification, a date code (year and week), a revision code and a pin 1 (or ball A1) mark; other optional marks used through the supply chain may also appear. Parts marked ES or E are engineering samples, not qualified and not approved for production use; ST's quality department is consulted before using them for a qualification run.
Dpad is the copper pad diameter and Dsm the solder mask opening for the BGA and WLCSP land patterns. The WLCSP top, its wafer back side, carries an A1 orientation dot.

The maximum junction temperature follows from the ambient temperature, the package's junction-to-ambient resistance and the dissipation, which is the internal power (IDD × VDD) plus the output pins' power with each pin's real low and high output levels and currents in use. ΘJA is measured per JESD51-2 (natural convection, still air).

With the internal reset off, the power-on and power-down reset (POR/PDR) is disabled, the brownout reset (BOR) is kept disabled, the programmable voltage detector (PVD) is disabled, VBAT no longer works and the VBAT pin is tied to VDD, and over-drive is not available. An external supply supervisor then allows VDD/VDDA down to 1.7 V.
